newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat meets Israeli president Weizman.
newsitem.headline: Arafat meets Israeli president Weizman.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and Israeli President Ezer Weizman met on the Israel-Gaza border on Tuesday in a bid to jolt ailing peace moves from seven weeks of crisis.

The meeting, only the second high level Israeli-PLO contact in nearly two months of deadlock, came as Israel's closest Arab peace partner Jordan snubbed Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in a dispute over water.
"We are going to discuss the problem of ice -- how to break that," Weizman, whose post is largely ceremonial, told reporters before the meeting.
Arafat downplayed hopes for a breakthrough, telling reporters: "The most important thing is having this meeting".
But Weizman, accompanied by Netanyahu's personal envoy Yitzhak Molho, said the meeting was not just a formality: "If there was nothing practical, I wouldn't come here."

Israeli-Palestinian peace talks plunged into deep freeze when Netanyahu gave the green light to bulldozers to break ground for a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem on land claimed by both sides, sparking a fresh cycle of violence.

Palestinians have turned to Weizman in the past to press the right-wing Netanyahu to show flexibility. Weizman, an architect of Israel's 1979 peace treaty with Egypt, has no formal political power but is widely respected in Israel.

Embarrassing the Israeli prime minister, Jordan said it called off a meeting between Crown Prince Hassan and Netanyahu after disagreements over water supplies Israel promised to the Arab kingdom under a 1994 peace treaty.

In what Netanyahu hoped would be a showcase Israeli-Arab meeting, he and the crown prince were to jointly attend a memorial ceremony for seven Israeli schoolgirls killed by a Jordanian soldier in March.
Jordan accused Israel of backing out at the last minute from an accord to fulfil its peace treaty pledge to help parched Jordan find an extra 50 million cubic metres of water a year.
Israel had promised 150 million cubic metres of water to Jordan under a 1994 peace deal. It has so far transferred only 50 million cubic metres.

Israeli Infrastructure Minister Ariel Sharon told Israel Radio he had proposed a plan to provide a second allotment of 50 million cubic metres of water six months ago but accused Jordan of raising unspecified new demands.
Netanyahu called the dispute a "mini-crisis" which he believed would be overcome.
Tuesday's meeting between Arafat and Weizman will be followed by a new mediation mission by U.S. peace envoy Dennis Ross, who is due in the region on Wednesday.
Ross will have to contend with a refusal by Israelis and Palestinians to budge from positions which snarled peacemaking two months ago.

The PLO demand Israel a freeze in settlement building including the East Jerusalem construction. Netanyahu wants the Palestinian Authority to crack down on "terrorism" as a condition for returning to negotiations after a Palestinian bomber blew up a Tel Aviv cafe on March 21, killing himself and three Israeli women.
In the West Bank, Israeli police removed dozens of Jewish settlers from a shack near a Jewish settlement and destroyed it along with two other wooden structures which they said were built illegally.
Several settler children were injured by shards of glass and 18 settlers were arrested.
The National Religious Party, which has nine of the 66 seats Netanyahu commands in the 120-member parliament, threatened to bolt the coalition if Netanyahu continued such actions.
